Actually, for $c_i = (k \cdot i) \pmod N$, the diagonal conditions are:
1. $c_i - c_j = i - j \implies k(i-j) \equiv i-j \pmod N \implies (k-1)(i-j) \equiv 0 \pmod N$.

2. $c_i - c_j = -(i - j) \implies k(i-j) \equiv -(i-j) \pmod N \implies (k+1)(i-j) \equiv 0 \pmod N$.
   This implies $k \equiv -1 \pmod N$ or $i \equiv j \pmod N$.
   So we need $k \not\equiv -1 \pmod N$.
